title: Dining layouts and table clearances
intro: Dining layout starts with people and use scenarios. Compare table forms, map moving chairs and doors, and distinguish chair operation from a usable circulation route.

sections.title: Define users and table form
sections.text: Record daily and guest counts, actual chair models and access needs. Rectangular and round tables do not become interchangeable merely by seating the same number: legs, bases and chair widths affect usable positions. Draw actual chairs and check entry and knee space. For an extending table, prepare both closed and extended layouts.
sections.caption: Compare actual seating positions, bases and use states.

sections.title: Separate chair movement from circulation
sections.text: Draw the chair stored, occupied and pulled back for standing, then add the walking route and room/sideboard door swings. Empty space with a tucked chair does not prove passage when it is pulled out. Test credible simultaneous states. If serving blocks access, revise position, dimensions or service arrangement and record why.
sections.caption: Check passage in the relevant occupied and moving states.

sections.title: Calculate an explicit layout envelope
sections.text: Exercise only: a 900 mm wide top with an assumed total movement zone of 1000 mm measured from each side edge needs ⁦1000 + 900 + 1000 = 2900⁩ mm. In a 3000 mm room, the arithmetic remainder is 100 mm. This is a geometric difference, not proof of comfort or accessibility. Verify the assumed zones against actual chairs, users, openings and project requirements.
sections.caption: 2900 mm follows the exercise assumptions; it is not a universal clearance.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The 2900 mm exercise envelope fits within 3000 mm, but an open sideboard door intersects an occupied chair. Reject approval based on arithmetic alone; relocate the sideboard and retest chair movement and serving together.
example.decision: Decision: resolve the door conflict, then repeat the movement check.

quiz.question: The arithmetic fits but a door hits a chair. What next?
quiz.explanation: Dimensional fit does not prove conflict-free operation.

assignment.prompt: Submit daily/guest layouts, moving-chair and door envelopes, the exercise calculation and a conflict log.

faq.question: Is the 1000 mm zone a universal rule?
faq.answer: No. It is an exercise assumption that must be checked against actual use and project requirements.
